note:
Regenerated 2026-11-10 for part 2 of the December 2026 email redesign (Doug's go on 2026-11-09, "do all now", and his update of the same day: Buttondown now sends with its Classic template, and the brand line stays at the top; the Dec 1 issue, featuring February, is the first to carry it), all 12 months, because the first screen and every card change. What changed: (1) the first screen is one brand line ("🌍 WanderGrade", no tagline) and one paragraph straight above the top card, "N best-value trips for {Month}, graded A+ to F on money, safety, weather and flights. 💵 marks where your dollar goes further than usual right now. Going another month? Pick your travel month →" (N the number of picks, the 💵 sentence only when a pick has the dollar line): the tagline, the old intro, the 📅 box and the "Top picks" heading are gone; (2) the Overall grade is a solid badge after each country's name (top card, compact cards, gems) in the site's own grade colours (public/styles.css .grAp to .grF), outside the name's link, and "— Overall" is gone; (3) the top card's grade row keeps its words and loses "per US State Dept", which becomes a 12px line under it, "Safety grade from US State Dept advisories"; compact cards and gems show letters only ("💰 B+ · 🛡️ A · 🌤️ A · ✈️ B", each icon held to its letter by a non-breaking space) and name a government only where it is not the edition's main one; (4) every card has the same two money lines, price first: "Prices ~73% below US levels" (the site's three bands, no 💰, no ", but graded worth it") and, from 3%, "💵 Dollar goes ~5% further than usual"; (5) a grade key opens the footer ("Reading the grades: …", newsletter._grade_key, each clause tied to the scoring code) and the footer's brand line reads "WanderGrade grades every country A+ to F · once a month, no spam · wandergrade.com · unsubscribe"; (6) compact cards load their photo at 220x168 (the payload's new photo_thumb, picks._banner's "thumb") instead of the 1024x420 banner; (7) for the Classic template no image has a side margin (a flag's gap is a non-breaking space and 3px on the name's link), every block of words has its own font-size and line-height, the intro

and the heading have their own margin, and each arrow is held to the word before it. The subject and the hidden preheader are unchanged, and so is what goes out: main 7a1491f's code builds the same payload as this tree for all ten editions x 12 months but for photo_thumb (test_digest_variants 1). The body is held to its own payload, line by line and badge by badge (scripts/digest_check.py), not to an older text. Earlier note: Regenerated 2026-11-10 for part 1 of the December 2026 email redesign (Doug's go on 2026-11-09, "do all now", after that day's newsletter review; the Dec 1 issue, featuring February, is the first to carry it), all 12 months, because every card changes. What changed: (1) the "Photo: …" line under each card is gone and one credits block sits under the closing quote, above the footer's border: "Photos (cropped) via Wikimedia Commons. {Country}: {photographer}, {licence} · …", one entry for each card that shows a photo, in card order, the photographer's name linking to the photo's file page and the licence to its text, 12px/18px, #6f6f6f, centred (why one block is enough, and why "(cropped)": the note above newsletter._credits); (2) the closing quote is a

at the 16px/24px Buttondown always delivered its

at, and its byline is 12px #666, the size of the credits; (3) the footer is two

s at 12px/18px in #666 (was #888) without "Photos via Wikimedia Commons.", its two links #666 and underlined; (4) the 📅 box, the Hidden gems sub-line, the "On a budget?" line and the reply line are
s with their own size, line height and margin (13px, 13px, 14px, and 14px/21px #444 with its hello@wandergrade.com link the same colour, underlined), so the intro is the only

left, and "per US State Dept" is #666 (was #888); (5) every text link's words sit in two spans with the colour on the inner one (newsletter._link), which Buttondown's a{color:…!important} can't reach: country names, "See the guide", "Pick your travel month", the cheapest-countries link and gem names stay green. Nothing else moved: a one-off script that rewrote exactly those pieces in the text main 7a1491f renders gave this tree's text byte for byte in all ten editions x 12 months (120 renders, every one of which differs before the rewrite), and the two trees build identical payloads. The subject and the hidden preheader are unchanged. The tests changed with it: bodies are no longer compared with 4788fd2's less stripped pieces (digest_snapshot's REVIEW3, COVERS, CHEAP_LINK, the cost-line and weights grafts and the subject mapping are gone, since the rest of the redesign changes nearly every piece of the body). Instead test_digest_variants holds every edition's payload, subject and preheader to 7a1491f's (digest_snapshot.BASE, its code on this tree's data), reads every email back against its own payload (scripts/digest_check.py: each visible line, link, image and credit) and checks the markup Buttondown can't restyle, and test_send_digest holds every Buttondown call and printed line to 7a1491f's with each body swapped for a token. Earlier note: Regenerated 2026-11-04 for the 2026-11 wording (Doug's 2026-11-03 decision; the Dec 1 issue, featuring February, is the first to carry it), all 12 months, because the subject moves in every one: the subject leads with the month ("🧭 {Month} trips: where your dollar goes furthest", was "🧭 Where your dollar goes furthest this {Month}"; plain ASCII after the emoji, so find_sent's needle stays inside it, test_send_digest 22), the preheader opens "Plan ahead:" and names the month ("… in N of {Month}’s picks." / "… and flights for {Month}.", was "… this month’s picks — here’s where it’s worth going." / "… this {Month}."), the intro ends "{Month}’s standouts" (was "This month’s"), the 📅 sentence reads "{Month} picks, sent two months ahead so there’s time to plan and book." (was "Featured for {Month} — about two months out, the sweet spot for booking.") and the hero fare's basis reads "({Month} vs the route’s usual)" (was "this month vs"). Nothing else moved: with only those pieces taken out (digest_snapshot.REVIEW3's pre, standouts, cal and basis groups) and the base's subject mapped to the new wording (digest_snapshot.subject_as_new, which must then equal this tree's exactly), every month's subject and text equal the base's in all ten editions x 12 months (120 renders, every one of which differs before the stripping), the base being main 3a35b13 (the Nov 9 batch and the guide layout fix, as shipped on 2026-11-06), re-checked on it that day when this wording landed, the hashes unchanged (its USD text is the hashes this file held before); the --against 4788fd2 comparisons (test_digest_variants, test_send_digest) take out the same groups and map the same subject. Earlier note: Regenerated 2026-11-06 when main (0e2dd88: the newsletter cover rule, the guide query redirect and the activity thumbnails) was merged into nov9/integration: all 12 months recomputed on the merged tree (scripts/digest_snapshot.py --variants USD, digest_hashes). Months 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 keep main's values; months 3, 5, 6 differ from main because of nov9's full climate.json rebuild alone (main's code rendered with the merged tree's climate.json gives the same 12 hashes), the months its 2026-10-28 note below names. Earlier notes (main's and nov9/integration's, joined in date order): Regenerated 2026-10-30 (later) for months 5, 7 and 8 only: Doug's cover overrides of that day (activities.json "photo" now on DJ FK GL GQ MW PY TG UG MY plus GB Tower Bridge, RO Bran Castle and PT Pena Palace; CG's Lefini override dropped for its gallery lead) move Portugal's cover from Belém Tower to Pena Palace, the only frozen pick they touch; with covers and credits taken out (digest_snapshot.COVERS) those months' subjects and text are unchanged and no other month moved. Earlier note: Regenerated 2026-10-30 for the newsletter cover rule, all 12 months: a pick's cover is now the first photo the site's own checks pass among activities.json "photo" (kept only as an optional override, on CG DJ FK GL GQ MW PY TG UG MY at the time) and the first six entries of its guide gallery (picks.cover_for), where it was "photo" alone. Under the fakes (digest_snapshot.fake_cover by title, fake_cover_file by a pinned file's name) the cover moves for 12 of the 17 countries the frozen months pick: TH Wat Arun (the fake's no-photo) -> Wat Rong Khun, VN Ha Long Bay -> Ho Chi Minh City, AR Buenos Aires -> Perito Moreno Glacier, CL Torres del Paine -> Valparaíso, MY Batu Caves (no-photo under the fake, so the fallback) -> George Town, Penang, MA Marrakesh -> Jemaa el-Fnaa, IN Taj Mahal -> Hawa Mahal, PL Kraków -> Wawel Castle, GR Santorini -> Acropolis of Athens, PT Lisbon -> Belém Tower, HU Budapest (no-photo) -> Heroes' Square, Budapest, LK Sigiriya (no-photo) -> Temple of the Tooth; PH, CN, EG, HR and MX keep theirs, and every month features at least one that moves. Nothing else moved: with each cover image (the hero's , a compact card's thumbnail cell) and "Photo:" credit line taken out (digest_snapshot.COVERS), every month's subject and text equal main's (53ce450) in all ten editions. test_digest_variants checks every edition's covers are digest_snapshot.fake_rule_cover's picks, and the --against 4788fd2 comparisons (it and test_send_digest) take covers and credits out of both texts, so graft_photos is gone. Regenerated 2026-10-30 for month 2 only: Malaysia's cover title (activities.json "photo") is now "Batu Caves", since "Petronas Towers" resolves to the towers' logo, so the fake cover keyed on the title changes (for "Batu Caves" it is one of the fake's no-photo titles, so Malaysia's thumbnail and photo credit drop out of February's text); nothing else in any month moved. The --against comparisons give the old tree this tree's cover titles (digest_snapshot.graft_photos). Regenerated 2026-10-29 for the two green buttons' labels ("See ’s guide →", "See every country’s grades →"), now inside …: Buttondown's inlined a{color:#0069FF!important} had turned their white text blue on green in the delivered Oct 2026 issue. With those spans unwrapped (digest_snapshot.REVIEW3's btn/btnend) every month hashes to the 2026-10-28 values. Regenerated 2026-10-28 again when nov9/month-table merged onto review 3's copy below, for its full climate.json rebuild (build_climate on every committed row: 23 rows moved, Morocco now measured at Marrakech): months 3, 5 and 6 change and no other, the same three months that branch's own golden moved from the pre-rebuild climate.json (March: Morocco leaves the picks and the Philippines comes in; May: Portugal moves; June: Hungary moves). test_digest_variants and test_send_digest --against 4788fd2 render that tree on this climate.json. Regenerated 2026-10-28 for review 3's USD copy, the second deliberate change after the /cheapest line: each 🛡️ grade names whose level it is (" per US State Dept", or the government that filled the gap), the AI callout drops "New:" and names ChatGPT, Claude, Grok or Perplexity, "route’s" takes the typographic apostrophe, and an explicit --month issue prints its month's next occurrence (render_cheapest.year_for: on the snapshot's 2026-10-03, months 1-9 read 2027 with the quote for 2027, where they read 2026). scripts/digest_snapshot.py on 4788fd2 (with this tree's cost line grafted) and on this tree: every month's text identical once CHEAP_LINK and REVIEW3's pieces are taken out of both; test_digest_variants --against 4788fd2 asserts that, and that each piece is in this tree's text where it belongs. Regenerated 2026-10-24 for the USD edition's new line after the hidden gems: 💰 On a budget? (💸 until the same day, Doug's pick) "The cheapest countries to visit in →" linking https://wandergrade.com/cheapest/ for the issue's month (scripts/digest_snapshot.py on HEAD 4f15187 and on the change: every month's text identical once that one paragraph is removed; test_digest_variants --against 4788fd2 compares with it taken out). Regenerated 2026-10-14 again for the tie rule (a tie on the shown score breaks on the unrounded one, then the name; list order used to decide). Regenerated 2026-10-14 for the default priorities moving to every factor Med (picks.WEIGHTS afford 3 -> 2; affordability had been High since the FX-tracker days). Re-checked 2026-10-04 after the cost line moved to the site's ±10% band on the printed decimals (newsletter._pl_band): unchanged, because on these frozen fixtures the five countries that change band (DK, FO, GB, LU, MH) are never a USD pick printed with a cost line. scripts/test_digest_variants.py --against 4788fd2 asserts both facts.
